newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast inflation falls to 5.0 pct in May.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast inflation falls to 5.0 pct in May.

text.p: Consumer prices in Ivory Coast rose by 0.3 percent in April from May, giving a year-on-year inflation rate of 5.0 percent, down from 6.1 percent in April, data from the National Statistics Institute (INS) showed.
This benchmark rate is calculated from separate indices for blue-collar and white-collar workers, accounting respectively for 80 percent and 20 percent of the so-called "combined index".
The government's aim is to hold inflation below three percent this year.
The INS did not provide any further information on the combined index.
It published the following provisional data:
BLUE COLLAR INDEX May April May 1996
The INS said the two indices were pushed up by a rise in food prices, offset to some extent by lower prices in the utilities component.

It also calculates an index for "European" households. This showed a fall of 0.9 percent in May from April, giving a year-on-year rate of 2.9 percent, down from 4.7 percent in April. Lower food and utilities prices explained the fall on the month. -- Alan Raybould, Abidjan newsroom +225 21 90 90
